subject: Segmentation & SLA prioritization — reserved GPU scope recap
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation & SLA prioritization — reserved GPU scope recap

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick written recap so we have aligned expectations and clear next steps. I captured the items we discussed and flagged a few open questions for the technical follow-up.

Key pain points you described
- Peak inference bursts for patient-facing features (NLP extract + summarization) cause tail spikes that impact perceived latency.
- Regulatory constraint: PHI must not leave your VPC; isolation and auditability are mandatory.
- Cost pressure: need predictable unit cost for budgeting but retain headroom for short bursts.

Goals you set
- 99th percentile generation latency under 250ms for the 1–2k token path with typical concurrency of 120 qps and burst to 300 qps for 2–3 minutes.
- Fully isolated reserved pool (no multi-tenant co-location) with KMS integration and audit logs for all inference requests.
- Production rollout in Q3; start with a 30-day pilot to validate tail latency and autoscale behavior.

Preliminary capacity & design thoughts (Rough; engineering to confirm in tech deep-dive)
- Suggested starting pool: 6 x A100 80GB-equivalent instances (reserved) with a 20% burst buffer to handle concurrent peaks; we can present alternate configurations (8 x smaller GPUs) at the tech call.
- Isolation: Dedicated tenant lanes + VPC peering into your network; Redwood Private control plane with customer-managed KMS.
- SLA targets to propose: 99.9% uptime for the reserved pool, latency SLO: 99p < 250ms for configured model variant under baseline load.
- Fallback policy: on pool saturation, route non-PHI requests to a hosted-compatible model variant to preserve availability.

Open questions for our engineering deep-dive
1) Typical request size distribution (tokens per request) beyond the 1–2k path? A short histogram from your prod logs would help sizing.
2) Acceptable trade-offs for quantization (int8 vs int4) on quality — are you willing to run a quick eval set if we propose aggressive quantization for cost reduction?
3) Procurement cadence: is a month-to-month pilot acceptable before we provision a longer reserved commitment?

Immediate next steps
- We will send a capacity estimate spreadsheet (attached) with 2 configuration options by EOD today.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML infra folks (propose Wed 5/27 or Thu 5/28, 10–11am PT).
- Share SOC2 evidence and private deployment checklist (Ben will attach the SLA doc).

Attachments: infrastructure-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — I’ll leave action items below.

--
Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before the tech call: 

1) Our current production 75th/95th/99th token histograms are attached below (Priya will forward the longer dump); median requests are ~300 tokens, 95p ~1,100, 99p ~1,900.
2) For the pilot we want to limit costs: would you be open to a month-long trial with usage-based billing + a capped reserved baseline while we validate latency behavior? If yes, we can accelerate procurement.
3) Security: KMS + audit logs are hard requirements for any reserved deployment. Can Redwood provide a sample audit log extract and an outline of log retention controls in advance of the deep-dive?

We’re available for Wed 10:00am PT for a 60-minute technical session — Priya, Alex, and our infra lead (Miguel) will join.

Alex / Priya — adding a few specifics from the ops side ahead of the deep-dive. Apologies for the quick note, wanted to clarify the items you called out.

On the pilot model and pricing
- We can do a hybrid pilot: a small reserved baseline (billed as a short-term commitment) + usage overage billing for bursts. That lets you validate the 99p latency without a long-term commit. I’ll surface sample pricing tiers in the deep-dive.

On audit logs & retention
- Redwood Private will push request-level logs to your S3 (or our forwarded S3) with per-request metadata (model, model_version, latency_ms, request_id, sha256(payload) for integrity). Retention is configurable; default package we propose is 90 days, we can extend to 1 year for compliance reasons. Sample log schema attached in the SLA doc.

On isolation and scaling
- For strict tenant isolation we’ll allocate dedicated GPUs (no colocated tenants) and dedicate ingress lanes. Autoscaler will allocate burst capacity from a reserved burst pool (pre-warmed nodes) with a target spin-up time of ~60–90s for additional instances; we’ll demonstrate a live spin-up test in the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (PDF)

Proposed next steps
- Confirm Wed 2026-05-27 10:00am PT for the 60min deep-dive — we will invite infra/MLops and solution engineering.
- Alex/Priya: please share the prod histogram dump and a short list of IP allowlist / networking constraints.
- Redwood: bring a clear cost comparison (reserved baseline vs. burstable + example savings with caching/quantization).

Thanks — Ben

- Pilot approach: 30-day reserved baseline + usage overage billing for bursts (we agreed this morning).
- Isolation: dedicated GPUs with KMS-managed keys and audit logs pushed to our S3 bucket.
- SLA discussion will cover uptime targets and latency SLOs (we want explicit remedies / credits for sustained breaches).

See you Wednesday.
